brief_summary: Two vertical travel rulers comparing post-actuation runway: a standard 4.0mm-travel switch with a 2.0mm actuation point leaving a 2.0mm runway to bottom-out, versus a 3.3mm-travel switch whose pre-travel is not published but whose runway is bounded at 1.3mm or less by the published total. Makes the runway concept concrete without inventing an unpublished pre-travel split for the Akko switch.
data_sources: https://cdn.sparkfun.com/assets/a/9/b/6/2/MX2A_RED-Datasheet-EN_US.pdf — Cherry MX2A Red: 2.0mm pre-travel, 4.0mm total travel
shortened-travel-switches-deep-dive.mdx § 'The runway: why distance matters as much as force' — 'the remaining runway cannot exceed 1.3mm, and in practice sits close to it'
warnings: Right-hand actuation tick position (aligned at the same height as the left ruler's 2.0mm mark) is an illustrative placeholder for comparison, not a measured value — labeled explicitly as unpublished in both the SVG and the caption.
